text:
Vegas won this one on the power play, and the numbers say they earned it. Mitch Marner finished it 2:40 into overtime with a snap shot on the man advantage, set up by Mark Stone and Trevor Connelly, to make it VGK 2, LAK 1. The Golden Knights went 2 for 3 with the extra man, Los Angeles 1 for 3, and the one clean separator was the second period.

That period was lopsided. Vegas generated 1.50 expected goals to the Kings' 0.32, and Connelly cashed one of those chances at 2:37 with a power-play snap shot off feeds from Stone and Marner. Artemi Panarin answered at 6:21 with a wrist shot, also on the power play, a goal that carried only a 9 percent chance of going in. Over the full game Vegas led in expected goals 2.81 to 1.91, and at even strength the gap was 2.40 to 1.30. In a simulated replay of every shot, Vegas wins 66 percent of the time.

Carter Hart stopped 26 of 27 against an expected 1.91 goals allowed, about 0.9 goals better than the shots called for, which kept Los Angeles from stealing it. Connelly put six shots on net in 14 minutes, and Stone's two assists made him the connective piece on both Vegas goals. Vegas also won 59 percent of the faceoffs and took the puck away seven times to Los Angeles's three. The Kings pushed back in the first period (0.73 to 0.64) and in overtime (0.36 to 0.15 in expected goals), but Marner's snap shot ended it on the one chance that mattered.
